ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING in prod.env and the failure is silent. Probed with docker compose config against two env files differing only in line order: with DATABASE_SSLMODE BEFORE NODES_DATABASE_URL the URL resolves to sslmode=disable; with it AFTER, compose resolves sslmode= to the EMPTY STRING and reports no error. libpq then falls back to its own default rather than refusing, so a mis-ordered file connects and nobody learns the TLS mode was never applied. An add-if-absent lane appends in whatever order the host's gaps dictate, so it can produce exactly that file.

Two env files differing only in the order of DATABASE_SSLMODE and NODES_DATABASE_URL produce different docker compose config output, one with sslmode=disable and one with sslmode= empty, and neither run reports an error.

PROD_ENV_MERGE cannot carry a value containing its own sed delimiter, and the failure has TWO forms. Probed directly: the substitution exits 1 with 'unknown option to s' and leaves the file byte-identical. In the SINGLE-KEY relay lanes the failed sed is the last command, so ssh returns 1 and the caller's set -euo pipefail aborts — loud, and the only form reachable today, because those are the only lanes carrying an operator-supplied value. In the MULTI-KEY block the remote loop has no set -e, so a later iteration's exit status overwrites the failed one: the loop exits 0, the lane prints its success line, and the key silently keeps its old value. That silent form becomes reachable the moment NODES_DATABASE_URL joins the multi-key block — which is exactly what the settings lane does.
The exact sed substitution from PROD_ENV_MERGE, given a replacement line containing a pipe, exits non-zero and leaves the target file byte-identical.

The settings lane must not be the place that fixes PROD_ENV_MERGE's delimiter hazard by rewriting the shared merge: tests/deploy/prodenvmerge_test.go pins that loop's exact text and requires exactly one copy of it. Either the hazard is fixed in the one shared definition with the test updated deliberately, or the lane refuses a value containing a pipe and says so — a silent no-op is the one option ruled out.
tests/deploy/prodenvmerge_test.go still asserts exactly one copy of the merge loop and still passes after whichever option is chosen.

The settings lane must compose NODES_DATABASE_URL with the sslmode value ALREADY RESOLVED — reading DATABASE_SSLMODE from prod.env and defaulting to disable — instead of emitting a literal ${DATABASE_SSLMODE} placeholder. Resolving on the host removes the ordering dependency entirely rather than documenting it. Thor's live value happens to have the same shape (sslmode=disable, no DATABASE_SSLMODE key present), but that is corroboration, not authority: it was written outside the deploy tooling during the #127 session and WHO wrote it — agent or human — is not recorded either way.
A prod.env that never receives a DATABASE_SSLMODE key still yields a fully-resolved sslmode in docker compose config, because the URL carries no placeholder.
